title: Careers and the World of Work
summary: Career fields, matching interests, abilities and values to careers, sources of career information, scarce skills in South Africa, and work ethics.

notes.text: In Grade 9 you will choose your subjects for Grades 10 to 12, and these choices affect which careers and studies are open to you. Thinking about your interests, abilities and values now helps you make good choices.

rows: What do I enjoy doing? Working with people, numbers, tools, nature, computers or ideas?
What am I good at? Which subjects do I do well in?
Am I outgoing or reserved? Do I like routine or variety?
What is important to me? Helping others, money, creativity, security, independence?
Nurse, doctor, pharmacist, social worker, physiotherapist
Electrician, civil engineer, IT technician, software developer
Agricultural scientist, environmental officer, game ranger, geologist

items: **University**: degrees (e.g. medicine, law, engineering) usually need a Bachelor's pass in matric and specific subjects such as Mathematics and Physical Sciences.
**TVET colleges** (Technical and Vocational Education and Training): practical qualifications such as electrical engineering, hospitality, office administration.
**Apprenticeships and learnerships**: learn a trade (plumber, welder, electrician) while working and earning.

notes.label: Scarce skills
notes.text: South Africa needs more people with skills in areas such as engineering, artisans (electricians, plumbers, welders), ICT, health sciences, teaching (especially Maths and Science) and accounting. Careers in scarce-skill areas usually have better job opportunities and bursaries.

items: School career counsellors and Life Orientation teachers.
Career expos and open days at universities and colleges.
Websites such as the national career advice portal (NCAP) and Khetha (Department of Higher Education).
**Job shadowing**: spending a day with someone at work.
Talking to people who work in a career that interests you.

notes.text: Employers look for people with a good **work ethic**: punctuality, reliability, honesty, a positive attitude, teamwork, respect, willingness to learn and taking responsibility.
